# Preface {.unnumbered}

I gave one of four
[keynote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keynote)
speeches at the May 2026 combined 
[meeting](images/ACMS-Poster.png)
of the 
[Christian Engineering Society (CES)](https://www.christianengineering.org)
and the 
[Association of Christians in the Mathematical Sciences (ACMS)](https://acmsonline.org). 

What follows is the keynote speech,
nearly exactly as delivered
in the Recital Hall 
of the Covenant Fine Arts Center
at [Calvin University ](https://calvin.edu)
on 29 May 2026.
Most of my slides, 
albeit with animations removed,
are interspersed throughout the text
as static images
to give readers a sense of the images
that accompanied the speech.
For the back story and 
a sense of the occasion beyond the slides, 
see my 
[blog post](https://matthewheun.com/posts/2026-05-29-ces-keynote-speech-photos/) 
about the keynote.

![Making a point. Source: Randy Pruim.](/images/CR5_0484-small.jpg){fig-alt="Making a point." group="ces-keynote-gallery" width=80%}

The pages that follow will make more sense if you
know a few things about the event:

1. I was introduced by my colleague and friend
   Jeremy Van Antwerp, to whom I refer
   several times during the speech.
2. I give reference to blue (backward) and 
   fuchsia (forward) signs to affixed to each row of seats
   in the auditorium. 
   The signs were labeled with "Engineering" or 
   "Mathematical sciences" to indicate 
   seating for audience members.
   The signs facilitated a few short discussions
   during the keynote.
3. Although this online version of the keynote
   includes chapters
   (Creation, Problems and the Fall, Redemption),
   I did not indicate the chapters during the speech.
   As you will read, 
   I offered small lego kits to attendees who could
   identify the "Creation, Fall, Redemption"
   structure of the speech.
   In fact, I gave away all five kits in 24 hours!
